You now have a set of methods you can use in every piece of academic work from here on. Each task you start is a chance to generate and organise ideas, each difficulty a prompt to try another approach, and each source an invitation to read for what it could mean. The habit to keep is simple: reach for a creative method when you are stuck, weigh more than one way forward, and read your sources beyond their surface.

That same habit carries into professional life. Wherever you plan work, meet a problem, or make sense of information, the people who do well are the ones who generate options, adapt, and see connections others miss. The creative methods you have just practised are ones you will use long after you graduate.
